All three were in the planned files and are explained in CHANGELOG and D162. tests/mirrors.rs has to change to compile (it matches exhaustively on Rule). run/tests.rs holds the producer-step tests for criterion 7. decisions.rs swaps the log guard's own parse for the shared decision_log_problems; its existing tests still pass. xtask/shard-timings.txt was listed but did not change, and no new test unit needs it.

findings.summary: CHANGELOG and D162 say 'the candidate gate' runs the rules; only the producer loop calls check_all at run time
findings.evidence: Grep finds runtime calls to check_all only in producer.rs:86 (mirror_drift_in). Nothing in crates/ is called a candidate gate. The repo test tests/mirrors.rs reads the base from git HEAD, so in a candidate tree it sees no diff, and the structure rules cannot catch drift left at the send-back limit at verification. The producer.rs doc comment still says drift left at the limit is caught by the repo test, which is not true for these two rules. The phrase repeats the accepted criterion's wording, so it is not counted against criterion 5.

findings.summary: The prompt rule's item-head matching can flag a renumbered item
findings.evidence: A numbered item's head is its first 24 characters, and joined_head accepts an alphanumeric character just before a match. If an added line renumbers `1. Do your role's job...` to `11. Do your role's job...`, the base head appears at offset 1 after a digit and is reported as a joined item. This is a rare edge case. A simpler guard would be to require that the match is not preceded by a digit when the head is numbered.

findings.summary: One rewritten doc comment line in producer.rs is longer than the surrounding 120-column wrap
findings.evidence: '/// Prompt files and new decision entries are among the files checked. Empty unless the work tree is Athena's own source: the registry' is about 137 characters. rustfmt does not reflow comments, so fmt passed.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the cause in the place it starts: the shared mirror registry in crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs, which the producer loop already runs before verification. Two rules are added there. `prompt structure` covers every crates/*/prompts/*.md file and reports a bullet or numbered item joined onto another line. `decision entries` covers docs/decisions.md and checks that each appended entry has a well-formed heading, the next id, and its own Provenance bullet. The existing append-only finding now names the entry it hit (`in D121`). The decision-log rules now live in one place that the CLI log guard also uses. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors` (45 passed), `cargo test -p athena-cli decisions` (12 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` (4 passed). The tests use the real broken shapes from both jobs, check the exact finding text, cover prose that must not be flagged and old log entries the change does not touch, and drive the whole producer loop to show each break is sent back with the file, the item and the fix, while correct edits land. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. Athena's "fails without the fix" runs (criteria 1, 3 and 7) failed at compile time, not on an assertion. Reading the code, removing only the new rule would make the tests' finding-count assertions fail. Remaining issues are minor: three planned files outside the deliverables list, all justified; a loose "candidate gate" phrase in CHANGELOG and D162; one rare false-positive case when an item is renumbered; and one long comment line.
